headlines.title: Out to gore the bullish Bush
Bush scores on honesty, Gore on understanding
BUSH BARELY AHEAD OF GORE IN FLORIDA AS RECOUNT HOLDS KEY TO THE ELECTION; Vice President Clings to Slim Edge in Popular Vote Nationwide
headlines.abstract: Winner of presidential election remains unknown full day after polls close; Gov George W Bush and Vice Pres Al Gore dispatch teams of lawyers to Florida to wrangle over handful of votes upon which their White House dreams now rest; incomplete vote count in Florida has Bush leading Gore by 1,784 votes, giving him lead in state of three one-hundredths of 1 percent of votes cast; even if Florida's 25 electoral votes are delivered to Bush, Democrats suggest they would pursue complaints about voting irregularites; in Palm Beach County, some Democrats are calling for new election, saying punch-card ballot was so perplexing that people mistakenly voted for Patrick J Buchanan, Reform Party candidate, instead of Gore; officials in Gore and Bush campaigns describe extraordinary series of events since election as nothing short of surreal; both Bush and Gore make brief appearances to address supporters; Bush says he expects Florida recount to confirm his victory, and Gore says outcome should not be hastily determined; photos; map; chart (L)

headlines.title: BUSH BARELY AHEAD OF GORE IN FLORIDA AS RECOUNT HOLDS KEY TO THE ELECTION; G.O.P. Retains Control, but Democrats Gain in Both Chambers
headlines.abstract: Democratic gains in House and Senate fall short of control but produce most narrowly divided Congress in almost half century; Democrats gain at least three Senate seats and one or two in House; with one Senate race undecided, Republicans have 50 seats and Democrats 49; in House, Republicans win apparent majority of 221 to 211, with 2 independents and one seat undecided; last time both houses were so closely divided was at end of 83d Congress of 1953-55, when Republicans ended with 49-to-46 Senate edge (with 1 independent) and House had 219 Republicans, 215 Democrats and 1 independent; photo (M)

headlines.title: THE 2000 ELECTION: THE RECOUNT; Bush Holds Slim Lead Over Gore as Florida Recounts
headlines.abstract: Associated Press reports that Gov George W Bush's lead in Florida has shrunk to 229 votes out of nearly six million cast, with 66 of state's 67 counties reporting; Florida secretary of state, Katherine Harris, says state has received official recounts from 53 counties, and that Bush holds lead in those counties of 1,784 votes; counties have until Nov 14 to send their official recounts to state election officials, although Harris asked counties to finish their recounts early; there is no suggestion that Harris, elected Republican loyal to Gov Jeb Bush, has acted in partisan fashion; photo (M)
